text: Plan: batch 1 is a broad screen of classic cross-sectional families (momentum at multiple horizons, short-term reversal, low vol, low beta, skewness, kurtosis, MA crossovers, 52wk-high proximity, market correlation, vol-scaled momentum), one representative per hypothesis since rank-weighted SR flips sign exactly under neg. Then refine winning families across neighboring lookbacks to require a parameter plateau (not a single-spike), test delayed versions to gauge decay robustness, then combine 2-3 independent robust families via add of cs_z components. Report a diversified composite plus the two most robust singles, favoring train-robust plateaus over peak train SR to maximize expected OOS Sharpe.

text: Findings: panel contains (a) cross-sectional momentum over t-10..t-3 with sharp reversal in last 3 days, robust across 5-15d windows and improved by scaling with std(40), and (b) a negative short-horizon skewness premium, robust across skew(5..20) with peak at 10-15d. LT reversal, low vol, low kurt exist but are weaker and dilute the composite. Blending adjacent parameters and both momentum forms, then combining the two families 1:1 after normalization, gave train SR 1.84-1.87; the composite survives 3-5 day delays (SR 1.13-1.23), supporting genuine persistence rather than train noise. Reporting three construction-diverse variants of the validated two-family composite: z-scored triple-momentum blend, z-scored double blend, and a pure rank version for outlier robustness.

rationale: Two robust families found via broad screen then neighborhood mapping: vol-scaled momentum over t-10..t-3 skipping the 3-day reversal window, and a negative short-horizon skewness premium (10-15d). Each is stable across adjacent lookbacks, both signs and magnitudes replicate under parameter perturbation, and the 1:1 normalized combination survives 3-5 day trade delays (SR 1.13-1.23 delayed vs 1.84-1.87 fresh), arguing genuine persistent structure. The three reported signals are construction-diverse blends of the same validated composite: triple-window z blend, double-window z blend, and a rank-normalized version for outlier robustness; parameter blending trades peak train SR for lower estimation variance to maximize expected OOS Sharpe.
